rows.evidence: Q1: Study Area and Results sections <U+2013> the authors develop the RASGEMINEC model and apply simulated annealing with EPANET to a real 191 ha citrus drip-irrigated network (385 hydrants) in Valencia, reporting their own model runs (Tables 1<U+2013>4) of energy consumption under three operating modes.
rows.notes: The study reports only energy consumption and instantaneous power requirements (2,049 vs 2,321 vs 2,423 kWh/day; 11.7% and 15.5% savings) computed from EPANET simulations of sectoring scenarios; the model outputs are not compared with measured energy or water data. It assumes a single irrigation set time (tr = 3.29 h) and a uniform application rate for all plots in the peak month, but it never evaluates, measures or discusses whether plots receive more or less water than required, nor any water-use inefficiency. The review's statement that uniform irrigation time causes inefficient water management is the review's own inference about the study's design, not a result reported by the study. No uncertainty measures, limitations on water use, or support conditions for the claimed water effect are given.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is an energy-optimisation modelling study of sector organisation in a pressurized drip network; water application adequacy is outside its scope.
